answer: Each identity runs one waterwheel on a ridge stream, locking a 75-credit bond to its wheel key. A spiral flume feeds it; an auditor recomputes power from flow and head, checks the power log, and burns the bond on a shortfall, reused key, or duplicate claim. The cedar wheel binds one identity; fees from one source rise: first 22, kth 22+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7015 and 1000 fakes cost 3,518,500 plus 75,000 locked bonds. An honest operator pays 22 once, recovering the bond after a clean epoch. A rented-wheel ring fails: one wheel cannot yield two logs for the same flow.
